classification.difficultyReason: Construct each derivative graph by translating tangent direction and steepness into signed heights. The hardest part combines the semicircle’s restricted domain, its horizontal tangent and its two vertical endpoint tangents to locate the zero and infer opposite unbounded end behaviour.

content.prompt: The diagrams below show sketches of $y=f(x)$. Sketch a graph of $y=f'(x)$.

spec.description: Symmetric smooth peak with two arrowed tails above a dashed horizontal asymptote. The plotting curve represents the qualitative sketch.

answer.short: Positive for $x<0$, zero at $x=0$ and negative for $x>0$. Both tails approach $y=0$.
answer.worked: Moving from the far left towards the maximum, the tangents start nearly horizontal, become steeper and then flatten again, so $f'$ has a positive hump and reaches zero at $x=0$. To the right the slopes become negative and then flatten towards zero, giving a negative dip.

spec.description: Positive left hump and negative right dip through the origin, with both tails flattening towards the horizontal axis.
Symmetric smooth valley with two arrowed tails below a dashed horizontal asymptote. The plotting curve represents the qualitative sketch.

answer.short: Negative for $x<0$, zero at $x=0$ and positive for $x>0$. Both tails approach $y=0$.
answer.worked: The curve slopes down to the left of the minimum, with nearly horizontal tangents far to the left and at the minimum itself. Draw a negative dip reaching zero at $x=0$. To the right the slopes are positive and flatten towards zero, giving a positive hump.

spec.description: Negative left dip and positive right hump through the origin, with both tails flattening towards the horizontal axis.
One decreasing branch in the first quadrant, with continuation arrows beside the positive vertical axis and above the positive horizontal axis.
spec.mathematics: The sketch is defined for $x>0$, decreases steeply near $x=0$ and flattens towards $y=0$.

answer.short: For $x>0$, the derivative rises from large negative values near $x=0$ towards $0$ from below.
answer.worked: The function decreases throughout the displayed domain, so its derivative lies below the horizontal axis. Near $x=0$ the downward tangents become arbitrarily steep. As $x$ increases they become nearly horizontal, so the derivative branch rises towards zero.

spec.description: Negative right-hand branch dropping beside the vertical axis and flattening just below the horizontal axis.
spec.mathematics: $f'(x)<0$ for $x>0$, with limits $-\infty$ at $0^+$ and $0$ as $x\to\infty$.

spec.description: One rising curve starting at the origin with a steep initial tangent and a continuation arrow to the right.
spec.mathematics: The given branch increases with decreasing positive slopes for $x>0$.

answer.short: For $x>0$, the derivative falls from large positive values near $x=0$ towards $0$ from above.
answer.worked: The tangents have positive slopes because the function rises. They are nearly vertical just to the right of $x=0$ and become flatter as $x$ increases. Draw a positive decreasing branch approaching the horizontal axis from above.

spec.description: Positive decreasing right-hand branch with arrows beside the vertical axis and above the horizontal axis.
spec.mathematics: $f'(x)>0$ for $x>0$, with limits $+\infty$ at $0^+$ and $0$ as $x\to\infty$.

spec.description: One logarithm-shaped branch with two arrows and a labelled horizontal intercept.
spec.mathematics: The branch for $x>0$ increases through $(1,0)$ and descends beside the vertical axis as $x\to0^+$.

answer.short: For $x>0$, the derivative falls from large positive values near $x=0$ towards $0$ from above.
answer.worked: The function is increasing for $x>0$, so the derivative is positive, including at $x=1$. The tangents are very steep near $x=0$ and become flatter to the right. Draw a positive decreasing branch approaching zero.

spec.description: Positive decreasing right-hand branch approaching both axes, with an arrow at each end.
spec.mathematics: $f'(x)>0$ for $x>0$, with limits $+\infty$ at $0^+$ and $0$ as $x\to\infty$.

spec.description: Upper semicircle with labelled horizontal endpoints and top height. No continuation arrows on the arc.
spec.mathematics: $x^2+y^2=1$, $y\geq0$, with endpoints $(-1,0)$ and $(1,0)$ and maximum at $(0,1)$.

answer.short: The derivative decreases through $(0,0)$ on $-1<x<1$. It tends to $+\infty$ as $x\to-1^+$ and to $-\infty$ as $x\to1^-$.
answer.worked: On the left half, the tangent slopes decrease from very large positive values to zero at the top. On the right half, the slopes are negative and become more negative towards $x=1$. Draw one decreasing branch through the origin between $x=-1$ and $x=1$. The vertical endpoint tangents give no finite derivative at either endpoint.

spec.description: Decreasing branch through the origin between dashed vertical asymptotes, with labels outside the branch.
spec.mathematics: The domain is $-1<x<1$. The branch tends to $+\infty$ at $-1^+$ and $-\infty$ at $1^-$.
